definition: a phrase used to introduce your personal opinion
example: From my perspective, working four longer days is better than five shorter ones.
collocations: from my perspective as a parent

definition: to be very sure that something is true or right
vi: tin tưởng mạnh mẽ, tin chắc rằng
example: I strongly believe that every neighbourhood needs a safe place for children to play.

definition: a phrase used to introduce a contrasting point
example: Living downtown is convenient. On the other hand, the rent is much higher.
collocations: on the one hand ... on the other hand

definition: a phrase meaning 'despite what I just said', used to add a contrasting point
vi: dù đã nói vậy, tuy nhiên
example: The course is expensive. Having said that, it helped me get a better job.
collocations: having said that, I still think

definition: a phrase used to add another point, often a stronger one
example: The apartment is close to my office. On top of that, it has free parking.

definition: a phrase used to introduce an example
example: There are many ways to save money; for instance, you can bring lunch from home.

definition: a phrase showing that something happened because of what was said before
example: The ferry was cancelled. As a result, we had to stay in Victoria another night.

definition: a phrase used to introduce a short summary at the end
example: To sum up, option A is cheaper, closer, and better for the whole family.

definition: a phrase used to support a point with something that happened to you
example: In my experience, people respond faster to a polite phone call than to an angry email.

definition: to agree with someone
example: My brother and I don't always see eye to eye on how to care for our parents.
collocations: see eye to eye on something
not always see eye to eye

definition: to have a friendly relationship with someone
example: I get along with most of my neighbours, especially the family next door.
collocations: find it hard to get along with

definition: to continue to communicate with someone
example: We keep in touch through video calls even though she moved back to Hanoi.
collocations: keep in touch with old friends

definition: to spend time with other people in a friendly way
vi: giao lưu, giao tiếp xã hội
example: Working from home means I have fewer chances to socialize with colleagues.

definition: influence from people of your own age or group to act like them
vi: áp lực từ bạn bè đồng trang lứa
example: Many teenagers start vaping because of peer pressure.

definition: to not want to do something and be slow to do it
example: Some employees may be reluctant to report problems because they fear losing their jobs.

definition: to be worried about something
example: It is natural to be concerned about how much time kids spend on screens.

definition: to support or agree with an idea or plan
example: Most residents seem to be in favour of turning the empty lot into a park.
collocations: be in favour of the proposal

definition: to disagree strongly with an idea or plan
example: Local businesses are likely to be opposed to the new parking fees on Main Street.

definition: having doubts that something is true or will work
example: At first I was skeptical about online therapy, but it really helped me.

definition: to make someone agree to do or believe something by giving reasons
example: I tried to persuade my friend to choose the cheaper apartment near the SkyTrain.

definition: an agreement where each side gives up something they wanted
example: We reached a compromise: I'll drive on weekdays and he'll drive on weekends.

definition: the advantages and disadvantages of something
example: Let's weigh the pros and cons before we decide to buy a car.

definition: a disadvantage or problem
example: The main drawback of this job is the long commute.

definition: to be more important or greater than something else
vi: lớn hơn, vượt trội hơn (về tầm quan trọng)
example: In my view, the benefits of a four-day work week outweigh the costs.

definition: to consider something when making a decision
example: When choosing a school, you should take into account how far it is from home.

definition: a healthy division of time between your job and your personal life
vi: sự cân bằng giữa công việc và cuộc sống
example: I took a job with a lower salary to have a better work-life balance.
synonyms: balance between work and personal life

definition: to feel alone and cut off from other people
vi: cảm thấy bị cô lập, cô đơn
example: Many newcomers feel isolated during their first long winter in Canada.

definition: to meet socially
vi: tụ tập, gặp gỡ (bạn bè, gia đình)
example: Our old classmates get together for dinner every few months.

definition: to refuse an offer or invitation
example: I had to turn down the invitation to the wedding because I couldn't get time off.

definition: the feeling of being accepted and part of a group
vi: cảm giác thuộc về, gắn bó
example: Joining a local soccer team gave me a sense of belonging in my new city.

definition: ways in which people from different cultures think or act differently
example: Cultural differences in how people give feedback can cause confusion at work.

definition: to be accepted by a group because you are similar to them
example: It took my son a few months to fit in at his new school.

definition: a situation where someone does not understand something correctly
example: There must have been a misunderstanding; I booked the room for Friday, not Saturday.

definition: during the time before something expected happens
vi: trong lúc chờ đợi, trong khi đó
example: The repair person will come on Monday; in the meantime, please don't use the dryer.

definition: a phrase meaning the answer changes according to something else
example: I'm not sure if I'll bike or take the bus tomorrow; it depends on the weather.

definition: a polite phrase showing that you understand someone's opinion, often before adding a different view
example: I see your point about the cost, but I still think the bigger apartment is worth it.

definition: a phrase used to say that an idea or explanation seems reasonable
example: "The bus has its own lane, so it's faster than driving at rush hour." "That makes sense — let's take transit, then."
collocations: that makes a lot of sense

definition: a phrase used before saying what you really think, especially something the listener may not like
example: To be honest, I'd rather stay home than go to a big party on a work night.

definition: a particular way of thinking about a situation; an opinion
example: From a parent's point of view, a later school start time would make mornings much easier.
collocations: see things from another point of view

definition: to meet or talk with someone you have not seen for a while and hear their news
vi: gặp gỡ hàn huyên, cập nhật tin tức với ai
example: I'm meeting my old classmate for coffee on Saturday to catch up with her.
collocations: catch up with someone over coffee
great to catch up with you

definition: to spend time relaxing with friends, often without a special plan (informal)
vi: đi chơi, tụ tập (với bạn bè)
example: On Friday nights, the teenagers usually hang out at the skate park near the rec centre.

definition: a phrase used to explain something again in a different or simpler way
example: The landlord said he was 'reviewing the rent'. In other words, it's going up.
collocations: to put it in other words

definition: polite, friendly conversation about unimportant topics, such as the weather
vi: chuyện phiếm, nói chuyện xã giao
example: In Canada, people often make small talk about the weather while waiting in line.

definition: to accept politely that two people have different opinions and stop arguing
vi: chấp nhận bất đồng quan điểm (và thôi tranh cãi)
example: My brother and I will never agree about politics, so we've decided to agree to disagree.

definition: a phrase meaning that you agree completely
example: "We need more crosswalks near the school." "I couldn't agree more."
collocations: I couldn't agree more with you

definition: to be willing to listen to and consider new ideas or other opinions
example: I wasn't sure about the new schedule at first, but I'm trying to keep an open mind.
collocations: try to keep an open mind
it's important to keep an open mind

definition: a phrase used to accept that what someone has said is reasonable, even if you do not fully agree
example: "I can't come because I'm working that day." "Fair enough, maybe next time."

definition: to give reasons or arguments that support an idea, plan or choice
vi: đưa ra lập luận ủng hộ (điều gì)
example: The parents want to make a case for a new crosswalk near the school, so they are collecting signatures.

definition: a phrase meaning 'in general' or 'considering everything'
example: There were a few problems, but on the whole, the community festival was a success.

definition: a word used to compare two facts or ideas and show how they are different
example: Option A is cheaper, whereas Option B is closer to public transit.

definition: a phrase meaning 'partly' or 'in some ways but not completely'
vi: ở một mức độ nào đó
example: I agree to some extent, but I don't think a higher fee will solve the parking problem.

definition: to seem to have a particular quality, based on how you behave or speak
vi: tạo ấn tượng là, có vẻ như là
example: He doesn't mean to be rude, but his short emails can come across as unfriendly.
collocations: don't want to come across as

definition: to start talking about a subject
example: I didn't want to bring up the noise problem at the barbecue, so I spoke to my neighbour later.

definition: to say or do something to make people feel more relaxed when they first meet
vi: phá vỡ sự ngại ngùng ban đầu
example: The organizers started with a fun game to break the ice among the newcomers.
collocations: a good way to break the ice

definition: to like each other and become friendly immediately (informal)
vi: hợp nhau ngay, ăn ý ngay từ đầu
example: My wife and our new neighbour hit it off right away because they both love gardening.

definition: to agree with someone or have the same understanding about something
vi: cùng quan điểm, thống nhất với nhau
example: Before we talk to the landlord, let's make sure we're on the same page about what we want.
collocations: make sure everyone is on the same page

definition: a reason or argument that is sensible and worth considering
vi: lập luận có cơ sở, ý kiến xác đáng
example: You make a valid point about safety, but the new bike lane would also reduce traffic.

definition: to support one person or group in an argument or disagreement
example: Most of the residents sided with the parents who wanted a crosswalk near the school.

definition: to accept or agree with an idea, plan or decision, even if you are not fully convinced
vi: làm theo, xuôi theo (dù chưa hoàn toàn đồng ý)
example: I wasn't keen on the restaurant they chose, but I went along with it to keep everyone happy.

definition: to defend or support a person, idea or right, especially when others are against it
vi: bênh vực, đứng lên bảo vệ
example: It takes courage to stand up for a coworker who is being treated unfairly.
collocations: stand up for what you believe in

definition: a phrase used to say that something is so obvious that it hardly needs to be said
vi: khỏi phải nói, hiển nhiên là
example: It goes without saying that safety should come first when planning a playground.

definition: a phrase meaning 'although'; used to introduce a fact that makes the main statement surprising
example: Despite the fact that the event was free, very few people showed up.
collocations: despite the fact that it was
despite the fact that many people
synonyms: in spite of the fact that

definition: a word used to accept that something is true, especially when it weakens your argument
example: Admittedly, the new community centre will be expensive, but it will serve the neighbourhood for decades.

definition: to gradually become less close to someone, often without any argument
example: After high school, my best friend and I slowly drifted apart.

definition: to persuade someone to do something
example: My coworker talked me into joining the office curling team, and I'm glad she did.

term: put yourself in someone else's shoes
definition: to imagine how you would feel if you were in another person's situation
vi: đặt mình vào vị trí của người khác
example: It's easier to be patient with newcomers if you put yourself in someone else's shoes and remember your own first year in Canada.
collocations: try to put yourself in someone's shoes

definition: to avoid talking about the main point, often because it is uncomfortable
vi: nói vòng vo, không đi thẳng vào vấn đề
example: Stop beating around the bush and tell me what you really think about the plan.

definition: to say honestly what you think, even if others may not like it
vi: nói thẳng suy nghĩ của mình
example: At the town hall meeting, the mayor said, "Please feel free to speak your mind about the new development."
collocations: feel free to speak your mind
not afraid to speak her mind

definition: careful not to say or do things that might upset or embarrass other people
example: Try to be tactful when you tell your neighbour that his dog barks all night.

definition: to argue against an idea, even if you actually agree with it, in order to test it or start a discussion
vi: cố tình phản biện (đóng vai người phản đối để thảo luận)
example: Just to play devil's advocate, what if the new bike lane makes traffic worse on Main Street?
collocations: play devil's advocate for a moment

definition: a word used to say that something can be stated with good reasons, even if not everyone agrees
vi: có thể nói là, được cho là
example: The seawall is arguably the most popular place to walk in the city.

definition: a phrase meaning 'after thinking about every part of the situation'
vi: xét mọi mặt, cân nhắc mọi điều
example: All things considered, I think the second option is the better choice for our family.

definition: to decide that something is true too quickly, before you know all the facts
example: Let's not jump to conclusions; maybe the package was delivered to the wrong unit.
collocations: be quick to jump to conclusions

definition: to admit, often unwillingly, that something is true or that someone else is right
example: I concede that the new bus route is slower, but it serves far more people.

definition: a formal phrase used to introduce an opinion or point that some people may hold
example: It could be argued that building more housing near transit would ease traffic problems.
collocations: it could also be argued that
it could be argued, however, that

term: give someone the benefit of the doubt
definition: to believe that someone is telling the truth or has good intentions, even if you are not sure
vi: tin tưởng ai đó, không vội nghi ngờ
example: He's usually reliable, so I'll give him the benefit of the doubt this time.
collocations: give her the benefit of the doubt
deserve the benefit of the doubt
be given the benefit of the doubt

definition: an argument or reason given to oppose another argument
example: A strong essay mentions a counterargument and then explains why it is less convincing.
